clue.text: Physicist showing new path he's worked out with chess piece

indicators.note: something worked out has been rearranged and solved, so the preceding words are reshuffled

blocks.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
the king is the most important chess piece

explanation.surface: A scientist demonstrates a fresh route he has devised for moving a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Hawking was the celebrated British theoretical physicist known for his work on black holes.

clue.text: Print lingo boss translated for football team

indicators.note: translating turns words into a different form, so these letters are recast in a new order

explanation.surface: A boss has some jargon printed in another language for the benefit of a football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporting Lisbon is the common English name for Sporting Clube de Portugal, a leading Portuguese soccer club.

clue.text: Point for example about registration mark's hidden feature

indicators.note: about means going round, so the abbreviation for example wraps the registration mark

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation, from Latin exempli gratia
short for registration; in Britain a car's age is given by its reg letter on the number plate

explanation.surface: A clue that seems to describe a mark on a registration document being concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition. EG goes round REG, after EAST.
explanation.definitionFit: In software and films, an Easter egg is a secret bonus or in-joke tucked away for users to discover.

clue.text: Trouble with fluttering lashes

indicators.note: fluttering things flap about restlessly, so the letters that follow are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone flirting with batted eyelashes is causing trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Hassle and trouble are everyday synonyms for bother, annoyance or difficulty.

clue.text: Occasionally negative, therefore receiving stick

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so the words for negative and therefore hold the stick

blocks.note: a wand is a thin stick

explanation.surface: Someone is sometimes pessimistic and so ends up getting stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick' reads as criticism in the surface, but here it is a thin rod; the two outer words take it between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase now and then means from time to time, at irregular intervals, just as occasionally does.

clue.text: Clever chart from which temperature is taken

indicators.note: something taken away is removed, so the letter for temperature disappears from the chart word

blocks.note: a table is a chart of figures

explanation.surface: A smart graph from which temperature readings have been removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Able describes someone competent and skilful, a common synonym for clever or talented.

clue.text: Very involved requirement in store

indicators.note: in places the requirement word inside the word for store

explanation.surface: Something that seems a key need when shopping, deep commitment notwithstanding.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion goes right after the first letter of the store word, a less obvious spot than the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Being knee-deep in something means being deeply engaged or embroiled in it, figuratively up to the knees.

clue.text: Sound from hooter, overwhelming one

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so the hooter word swallows the one

blocks.note: hooter is British slang for the nose

explanation.surface: A deafening blast from a horn drowning out someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise is a sound, typically a loud or unwanted one, so the two are general synonyms.

clue.text: Get through election mostly working for high-flying data collector

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the election word is dropped

blocks.note: to weather a storm is to get through it
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Surviving an election campaign with the help of a powerful data-gathering operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather balloon carries instruments high into the atmosphere to measure and record meteorological readings.

clue.text: So marsh, except for odd parts, happens to be fertile spot

indicators.note: leaving out the odd-numbered letters keeps only the even-placed ones of the words before

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A boggy area, apart from some strange bits, turns out to be good for growing things.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a green, watered area in a desert where plants can grow amid barren sand.

clue.text: Carnivore in rage, very unhappy, coming back with new energy

indicators.note: coming back means returning the way it came, so the first three pieces are read backwards

explanation.surface: A furious, miserable meat-eater returns with fresh vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: The wolverine is a stocky, fierce meat-eating mammal of the weasel family found in northern forests.

clue.text: Increasing taxation initially relating to jewellery

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

explanation.surface: Taxes going up, starting with a levy on jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Trebling means multiplying by three, a particular way of making something grow larger.

clue.text: Most unusual depth in poem by saint

indicators.note: in places the depth abbreviation inside the poem word

blocks.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A strange profundity in verse written by a holy figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' in a down-or-across charade means placed next to, so the saint follows the poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddest is the superlative of odd, meaning strangest, the same as most unusual or peculiar.

clue.text: Plots beginning to subvert Conservative policies

indicators.note: a beginning is the opening letter, here of the word following

blocks.note: a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party
a party line is a policy

explanation.surface: Conspiracies starting to undermine the policies of the Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Plots of novels or films are their storylines, the sequences of events in a narrative.

clue.text: End of annual period around Christmas

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the word that follows
turned around, the assembled letters run the other way

blocks.note: an eon is a long period of time

explanation.surface: The close of the year arrives with the holiday season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around Christmas' reads as a time of year, but 'around' is the signal to read L+EON backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is a traditional word for Christmas, from French Noël, seen on cards and in carols.

clue.text: Dignified arrangement of a quest set up without pressure

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the pressure abbreviation is removed
an arrangement puts things in a new order, so the following letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A stately plan for an expedition organised with no stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' looks like a reversal signal, but it is plain fodder: remove P from A QUEST SET UP and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Statuesque describes someone tall, poised and imposing, like a statue, which conveys a dignified bearing.

clue.text: Extract estimate of cost

blocks.note: first meaning: a passage taken from a text
second meaning: a builder's or supplier's price offer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Extract' looks like a verb, but here it is the noun for a cited passage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a passage repeated from a book or speech and a formal price given in advance for work.

clue.text: Doctor cares not for predecessor

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the following letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: A physician who does not care about the person who had the job before.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor is someone who came earlier in one's family line, a forebear or predecessor.

clue.text: Fruit began to go rotten in vehicle

indicators.note: going rotten means breaking down and decaying, so the word before is broken up
in puts the reworked letters inside the vehicle word

blocks.note: lorry is the British word for a truck

explanation.surface: Produce in a delivery truck has started to spoil.
explanation.definitionFit: The loganberry is a raspberry-blackberry hybrid, a soft red fruit.

clue.text: Search with horse covering miles

indicators.note: covering means going over and around, so the horse word encloses the miles abbreviation

blocks.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse

explanation.surface: A hunt on horseback ranging over many miles.
explanation.definitionFit: To comb an area is to search it thoroughly, as a comb passes through every strand of hair.

clue.text: Funny series? Some miss it completely

indicators.note: some means a portion, so the letters are a part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A comedy show that some viewers manage to overlook entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitcom is a situation comedy, a television series designed to be humorous.

clue.text: Meal, excellent, quietly consumed

indicators.note: consumed means eaten, so the soft-music letter is swallowed by the word for excellent

blocks.note: p for piano, the musical direction

explanation.surface: A fine dinner eaten in silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Supper is an evening meal, often a light one taken late in the day.

clue.text: Bit quiet, vocally

indicators.note: vocally means spoken out, so the word for quiet is judged by its sound

explanation.surface: Speaking a little more softly.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a bit or fragment of something, a portion of a whole.

clue.text: On the whole exhausted before melodrama's last lines

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the possessive word before it

explanation.surface: Overall, a cast is worn out before the closing lines of an over-the-top play.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom all in all means taking everything into account, broadly the same as on the whole.

clue.text: King unknown in middle of desert island

indicators.note: middle of keeps just the central letters of the following word
in places the king and unknown abbreviations inside the middle letters

blocks.note: the third and fourth of six letters
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

explanation.surface: A monarch, unidentified, stranded on a remote island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert island' reads as one phrase, but 'desert' is wordplay and 'island' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is a large island in the Inner Hebrides off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Passed area in open range

indicators.note: in places the area abbreviation inside the run of letters formed by open and range

blocks.note: ken is the range of one's knowledge

explanation.surface: Walking past a patch of open country.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken, meaning range of knowledge, survives mostly in the phrase 'beyond my ken'.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtaken means passed by someone moving faster, as a car goes by another on the road.

clue.text: Material from speech in order

indicators.note: from means taken out of, so the letters come straight out of the words that follow

blocks.note: the run across the three words

explanation.surface: Fabric pulled from a speech, set out properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Chino is a sturdy twilled cotton cloth, used for the trousers called chinos.

clue.text: Crime writer's odd gems one ignores

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of order, so the words that follow are jumbled

explanation.surface: A novelist's peculiar jewels that someone overlooks.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'; 'odd' looks like part of the jewels' description but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Simenon was the prolific Belgian novelist who created the detective Inspector Maigret.
